hypothesis: why does full-corpus own-retrieval (0.3869) still lag cdeotte source-matched (0.6086) despite measured recall@5=0.481 -- inspect actual retrieved text side by side
notes: Hand-compared cdeotte's context vs our own full-corpus BM25 context for the same 3 T1 rows (merged on prompt). Row 0 (Didymogenes classification question): cdeotte's context opens with 'Didymogenes is a genus of green algae in the class Trebouxiophyceae' -- nearly VERBATIM the correct answer text. Our own retrieval returned 'Ochromonas is a genus of algae...' -- a different genus entirely, still wrong even with the full 276k-article corpus (matches the Didymogenes example already flagged in the Day-2 mismatch-row work). Row 1 (NJ Transit Main Line color): cdeotte's context is on-topic (transit map colors); ours retrieved a gemstone color-naming taxonomy -- a lexical false-positive on the word 'color'. Row 2 (Big Mama Thornton): cdeotte's context explicitly names 'Blues singer Big Mama Thornton had a hit with Hound Dog'; ours retrieved 'Big mama' (a Chinese internet-censorship neologism) and 'Catherine Thornton' (an unrelated athlete) -- fooled by matching 'Big'+'mama'+'Thornton' as independent tokens rather than the single named entity 'Big Mama Thornton'. CONCLUSION: our BM25 retriever's bag-of-words scoring has no phrase/entity-level understanding and is getting fooled by partial keyword overlap on multi-word named entities -- a real precision problem distinct from corpus coverage (recall), and it did not improve when corpus coverage went from 20k to 276k articles because the failure mode is about RANKING within what's available, not about whether the right article exists in the index. This is a more actionable finding than 'recall wasn't enough' -- it points at phrase-aware/entity-aware retrieval (e.g. requiring exact multi-word phrase matches to score highly, or a reranker) as the next lever, not simply more corpus coverage. Whether cdeotte's context is this good BECAUSE it derives from the actual generating article (closer to true source-article ground truth than any retrieval this project has done) or from a genuinely better retrieval pipeline is not distinguished by this sample -- worth checking with more rows before concluding either way.

hypothesis: is the reader's near-baseline MAP@3 across every run in this project caused by a weak model/corpus, or by an optimization failure -- tested by whether the training loop can overfit 64 rows at all, and by what the loss value itself implies
notes: MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THE PROJECT. Every training run held its loss at ~1.61; ln(5)=1.6094 is EXACTLY the loss of uniform predictions over 5 options, i.e. the reader never demonstrably learned anything. scripts/diagnose_overfit_sanity.py swept lr in {5e-6, 2e-5, 5e-5} over 64 rows x 60 steps: min per-batch loss reached 0.6753, 0.1010, and 0.0018 respectively. Reaching 0.0018 PROVES the training loop, label alignment, and truncation='only_first' are all correct -- gradients flow and the randomly-initialized MC head can learn. So the cause is purely optimization scale: at lr=5e-6 with 10% warmup over 465 optimizer steps, the effective LR at optim_step 15 -- the step nearly every run in this project reported as its 'best checkpoint' -- is 1.63e-6, far too small to train a freshly-initialized AutoModelForMultipleChoice head (classifier.weight + pooler.dense.* are randomly initialized, visible in every run's own LOAD REPORT). Public 0.82-0.86 solutions used ~60k rows x 2 epochs at lr 1e-5..3e-5 = 10-20x more total learning. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the 'learn fast, forget fast' dynamic documented in DEVLOG.md and reports/ablation_table.md is NOT a real training dynamic, it is noise around a model near its random init; (2) row 3's 0.5641 and row 5's 0.6086 peaks are best-of-N-evaluations selections over that noise, plausibly riding row 1's measured options-only lexical shortcut (0.4780) rather than learned reading; (3) EVERY negative result that concluded 'X did not help the trained reader' -- phrase-match reranking, context length 384->768, the general-corpus swap -- was measured against a reader that could not learn, so none are refuted and all must be relabelled from 'resolved negative' to 'NOT YET TESTED'. notes: Kernel ougridd/day3-submission-ens scored FOUR configs on the same clean gold 200 and shipped only the winner. Results: single mgoksu/llm-science-run-context-2 0.8600 [0.8208,0.8967]; single sandiago21/llm-science-exam-deberta-v3-large-context-3 0.3800 [0.3292,0.4308] (essentially the 0.3667 baseline -- that public checkpoint is not a usable leg, whether because it is weak or expects a different input format; not investigated further given the deadline); ensemble mean-raw 0.8600 [0.8208,0.8967]; ensemble mean-znorm 0.7908 [0.7483,0.8317].
